data.title: Biological limits of lifespan extension: evidence for a shift from pathway leverage to system-level buffering across species
data.authors: Pirscoveanu DF; Papa MC; Kaltwasser B; Hermann DM; Brockmeier U; Cercel A; Oliver A; Grillari J; Ionica MV; Popa-Wagner A

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: mTOR/TOR pathway interventions achieve large lifespan extensions in simple organisms but face declining efficacy in mammals due to distributed multi-tissue buffering, redundancy, and pharmacokinetic complexity - proposing a unifying framework for the translational challenge of aging pathway targeting.
data.abstract_excerpt: Interventions targeting conserved aging pathways can markedly extend lifespan in model organisms, yet their efficacy declines with increasing organismal complexity. While this phenomenon is well documented, the underlying constraints remain poorly defined. Here, we integrate comparative experimental data with mechanistic insights to propose a unifying framework explaining the declining ceiling of lifespan extension.

extracted_findings.effect: Lifespan extension via mTOR inhibition declines with organismal complexity; mammals show system-level buffering that limits single-pathway leverage
